subject: ventures/ticket-resale-profit-calculator
professional: a full-time ticket broker who lists inventory across StubHub, SeatGeek, Vivid Seats and Ticketmaster resale (and, for the tax lines, a CPA who files for resellers). First checks: net payout after the seller fee, per-ticket vs per-order fees, break-even and target list price, whether cost basis includes the buyer fees paid at purchase, what happens to unsold inventory, and whether a pasted sales log is read correctly.

evidence.correctness: Pricing arithmetic is right on every case recomputed by hand. `node cli.mjs price --cost 100 --qty 4 --fee 15 --flat-fee 2.5 --delivery 10 --list 140 --json` gave sellerFee 94, payout 456, profit 56, roi 14, breakEvenList 123.53; by hand 560*0.15+4*2.5=94, 560-94-10=456, 456-400=56, 56/400=14%, (400+10+10)/(4*0.85)=123.529. `--target-profit 50` gave 138.24 (by hand 470/3.4=138.235). `price --cost 120 --qty 2 --list 150 --p-sell 0.8` gave expected -$24.00 and break-even sale chance 89% (0.8*30+0.2*-240=-24; 240/270=0.889). Sales log total on the fixture (`node cli.mjs log fixtures/sales.csv`) printed $899.75 profit, 19.02% ROI, 10.85% fees; an independent Python csv.DictReader sum gave 899.75, 19.022, 10.851. But a log line with unquoted money in thousands (`Concert,StubHub,2,$1,200.00,$1,500.00,$150.00`, the format engine.mjs:200 says is handled) is silently read as cost $1, gross $200 and reported as `1 sales netted $198 on $1 paid (19800% ROI)`, not skipped. A header with a `Purchase Date` column before `Total Cost` makes the whole log unreadable (exit 2). A silent wrong number on a documented input caps this at 2.
evidence.completeness: Every feature the README, page and llms.txt name was exercised and works end to end: price with --list, --target-profit, --flat-fee, --delivery, --p-sell, --salvage, --json; cross-marketplace table; `log` from file and stdin; per-platform profit/ROI/fee%; losing-sales list; --min-roi exit 1 gate (cli.test.mjs, 31/31 pass); page and guide link each other; usage opt-out present. No TODOs or stubs. Sales-log parsing works on the documented header and headerless formats but not on common real-world variants (see defects).
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/ticket-resale-profit-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: tests 31, pass 31, fail 0. Five seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 SURVIVED (dropping salvage from ifUnsold, engine.mjs:77; dropping the per-ticket flat fee from the break-even/target list price, engine.mjs:60; flagging losers on gross instead of payout, engine.mjs:185), 2 caught (fees not subtracted in the log parser; Ticketmaster preset 15->10). The break-even price with a flat fee, the core number a seller with a per-ticket fee relies on, has no test.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (202 lines), cli.mjs (105), index.html script, tests. Small, zero-dependency, pure functions; input validated with RangeError (CLI exit 2 on --fee 100, --qty 1.5, --p-sell 1.5, all verified); HTML escaped before innerHTML. Defects: header mapping takes the first column whose name matches a prefix regex (engine.mjs:112/149) so `Purchase Date` steals the cost column; comma is a field separator even inside unquoted money (engine.mjs:128) with no sanity check; summary text prints raw floats (`$4730 paid`, `$76.5`, engine.mjs:194); the page turns a blank field into 0 silently (index.html:159), so a cleared fee box becomes a 0% fee.
evidence.claims: No-warranty, not-tax-advice, trademark and privacy text present on both pages (page.test.mjs asserts them). Guide arithmetic checked: 1/0.9=1.111 ('about 11% above'), 1/1.125=0.889 ('about 89 in 100'), 0.8*(1+m)=1 gives m=0.25 ('a quarter of your cost'), 0.8*1.12=0.896<1 ('negative expected return'): all true. Unbacked: engine.mjs:200 'thousands separators are ignored' (false unless quoted, shown above); fee presets 'as last checked' (engine.mjs:17, README.md:21) carry no date and no source anywhere in the tree. llms.txt points at github.io URLs, but the Pages build rewrites hosts (source-only; served page could not be loaded: proxy 403), so not filed.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: an occasional reseller with 2 tickets at $120 can learn break-even ($133.33), payout at $150 on four marketplaces and that 80% sell-through makes it -$24 expected; that job is done. A full-time broker would hit in the first hour: pasting a marketplace export (header names vary, unquoted thousands) gives a wrong number or an unreadable log; no partial sell-through (order is all-or-nothing); no price-drop schedule over days to event; nothing tells them to put the buyer fees they paid at purchase into cost.
evidence.domain: Method matches broker practice: seller fee as a percentage of the list (buyer-side fees excluded and said so), per-ticket flat fee separated from per-order delivery, break-even = (cost+flat+delivery)/(qty*(1-fee)), expected value with a salvage value for unsold inventory. Fee presets 10/10/10/15 are within the range of seller fees publicly reported for US resale as I know them to mid-2026 (StubHub ~10-15% varying by event, SeatGeek ~10%, Vivid Seats ~10%, Ticketmaster fan-to-fan ~10-15%; not re-fetched, these change), so plausible but uncited. Tax: 'resale profit can be taxable income and marketplaces may report it' is consistent with IRC s.6050W and the 2025 OBBBA reversion of the Form 1099-K threshold to $20,000 and 200 transactions. A CPA would add that cost basis includes the fees paid when buying and that a loss on personal-use tickets is not deductible; neither is said.

defects.what: Unquoted money with thousands separators in a sales-log line ($1,200.00) is split on the comma and the row is accepted with shifted columns: cost $1, gross $200, '19800% ROI', instead of being skipped or flagged. The input notes claim this format is handled.
Input note 'Dollar signs and thousands separators are ignored' is only true for quoted CSV fields.
Header mapping takes the first column whose name starts with a cost/sale/event prefix; a 'Purchase Date' column steals 'cost' and the whole log becomes unreadable; 'Sold On' would steal 'sale'.
Break-even/target list price with a per-ticket flat fee, salvage value in ifUnsold, and the losing-sales filter are untested: three seeded mutants survived.
Fee presets (10/10/10/15) are described as 'as last checked' but carry no date or source anywhere in the tree.

Cost input 'Paid per ticket ($)' does not say to include the buyer/service fees paid when buying; the FAQ's 'Buyer fees ... are not in the maths' reads as excluding them, understating cost basis and overstating profit by the purchase fee (often 15-30% on primary).
A blank number field on the page silently becomes 0 (a cleared seller-fee box becomes a 0% fee).
Sell-through is all-or-nothing per order; selling some of the tickets, or a price-drop schedule toward the event, is not modelled.
Summary text prints raw floats ('$4730 paid', '$76.5').

verdict: A small, honest calculator whose pricing arithmetic is right: every hand-recomputed payout, break-even, target price, expected profit and fixture total matched (node cli.mjs price/log, Python re-sum). It does not meet the bar. The sales-log parser turns unquoted '$1,200.00' into a $1 cost and a 19800% ROI without a warning, against its own input note; a common extra header column empties the log; and 3 of 5 seeded mutants survive, including the flat fee in break-even. Fee presets are plausible but undated and unsourced, and the cost field never tells a seller to include the fees they paid buying. Fine for a casual reseller pricing one listing; a full-time broker pasting a real export would get a wrong number in the first hour.
